--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -241,9 +241,42 @@
-        cache_get = cache.get
-        for chunk in text_chunks:
-            chunk_ids = cache_get(chunk)
-            if chunk_ids is None:
-                chunk_bytes = chunk.encode("utf-8") # raw bytes
-                chunk_ids = self._encode_chunk(chunk_bytes, merge_lookup)
-                cache[chunk] = chunk_ids
-            ids.extend(chunk_ids)
-        return ids
+        missing = [c for c in dict.fromkeys(text_chunks) if c not in cache]
+        if missing:
+            ordered = self._get_ordered_merges(merge_lookup)
+            if ordered is not None:
+                # every merge produces an id larger than both of its inputs, so
+                # applying each merge once in index order matches _encode_chunk.
+                # the chunks are joined by a code point no merge uses, so no
+                # merge can cross a chunk boundary.
+                sep, pairs = ordered
+                s = sep.join([c.encode("utf-8").decode("latin-1") for c in missing])
+                for pat, rep in pairs:
+                    s = s.replace(pat, rep)
+                for chunk, part in zip(missing, s.split(sep)):
+                    cache[chunk] = list(map(ord, part))
+            else:
+                for chunk in missing:
+                    chunk_bytes = chunk.encode("utf-8") # raw bytes
+                    cache[chunk] = self._encode_chunk(chunk_bytes, merge_lookup)
+        extend = ids.extend
+        for chunk in text_chunks:
+            extend(cache[chunk])
+        return ids
+
+    def _get_ordered_merges(self, merge_lookup):
+        # merges as (pair str, id str) in index order, plus a separator code
+        # point, or None if the merges do not allow encoding this way
+        cached = getattr(self, "_ordered_merges", None)
+        if cached is not None and cached[0] is merge_lookup:
+            return cached[1]
+        ordered = sorted(self.merges.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
+        top = 255
+        result = None
+        if all(type(p0) is int and type(p1) is int and type(idx) is int
+               and 0 <= p0 < idx and 0 <= p1 < idx and idx < 0x10FFFF
+               for (p0, p1), idx in ordered) and \
+                len({idx for _, idx in ordered}) == len(ordered):
+            if ordered:
+                top = max(top, ordered[-1][1])
+            pairs = [(chr(p0) + chr(p1), chr(idx)) for (p0, p1), idx in ordered]
+            result = (chr(top + 1), pairs)
+        self._ordered_merges = (merge_lookup, result)
+        return result

actions.reason: Tried batching the uncached chunks in RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary: join them with a separator code point no merge uses, then apply each merge once in index order with str.replace. Outputs were identical on the equivalence harness, but encode_ir ratio was 1.0012 (400507669 -> 400977547), so per-chunk merge work is now only a few percent of the metric. Most of the remaining cost is interpreter startup, the regex module import and pattern compilation, plus the harness itself. The change also skipped GPT4Tokenizer's _encode_chunk override (byte shuffle) and failed 7 tests. Reverted; the tree matches the tip. No change found that reaches the 1% minimum without changing behaviour.

journal.text:
I tried batching the uncached chunks in RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary in minbpe/regex.py. The idea was to join them with a separator code point that no merge uses. Then each merge is applied once, in index order, with str.replace. The edit replaced lines 241-249 with 42 lines.

My sandbox evaluation of perf encode_ir was rejected. 7 stable tests failed, all of them GPT4Tokenizer encode/decode identity or tiktoken equality cases. Outputs were identical on the equivalence harness. The encode_ir ratio was 1.0012 (400507669 -> 400977547), so the change did not help. I reverted it, replacing the 42 lines with the original 9. I submitted nothing.

I now believe per-chunk merge work is only a few percent of encode_ir in this code. Most of the remaining cost is interpreter overhead, not merge application. Tightening the merge loop alone will not move the metric.

Next I will profile encode_ir to find where the interpreter time goes before changing anything. I will also work out why GPT4Tokenizer failed while the harness passed.
